newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says letter bombs not mailed in Alexandria.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says letter bombs not mailed in Alexandria.

text.p: Egypt denied on Saturday that letter bombs posted to the United States came from the Egyptian city of Alexandria, as suggested by some of the postmarks.
"Their source was absolutely not the city of Alexandria," said the interior ministry spokesman, Major-General Raouf el-Menawi, quoted in the government newspaper al-Ahram.

"Egyptian security organisations control and monitor terrorist activities and they have a high capability to discover such operations. Modern technology can be used to forge postmarks and so on," he added.

Menawi, who was speaking in Tunis, implied that his government took the suggestion that the eight letter bombs came from Egypt as a national insult. "Such accusations against people in Egypt are completely unacceptable," he said.
The newspaper gave no indication of whether the Egyptian police had examined the envelopes and drawn any conclusions.

The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) says five of the letter bombs were found in Washington and three in the area around Leavenworth, Kansas, the site of a federal prison holding one of the men convicted for the bombing of the World Trade Center in New York in 1993.

The Washington bombs were addressed to the offices of al-Hayat, a newspaper leased to Saudi Prince Khalid bin Sultan. Four bombs were found at al-Hayat's offices and the fifth turned up at the city post office.
The FBI has asked its legal attache in Egypt to travel to Alexandria, which was the postmark on some of the bombs.
